name: N'Djamena
subtitle: N'Djamena, capital of Chad: its numbers, a short history and places to see beyond the World Heritage list.

keyPoints.text: About 993,492 people live in N'Djamena (the 2009 census) (counted 2009).
N'Djamena was founded by the French in 1900 and was originally called Fort Lamy.
In 1973 President François Tombalbaye renamed the city N'Djamena as part of his 'Africanization' project.

parts.text: N'Djamena was founded by the French in 1900 and was originally called Fort Lamy.
In 1973 President François Tombalbaye renamed the city N'Djamena as part of his 'Africanization' project.
N'Djamena lies on the banks of the Chari River, directly across from Kousséri in Cameroon, and is Chad's chief export centre.
The Chari and Logone rivers meet near N'Djamena; both feed Lake Chad.
N'Djamena has ten arrondissements comprising 64 quartiers.
N'Djamena's population was 530,965 in 1993, or 8.5 per cent of Chad's population, according to the 2012 thematic synthesis.
Fort-Lamy already had a first mosque in 1910, in front of the governor's office, built with the colony's financial support.
A mosque was built from the local budget in 1939-1940 at the junction of the Ambassatna, Gardolé and Mardjandafack districts.
The Toumaï skull (Sahelanthropus tchadensis) was found on 19 July 2001 in the Djourab desert by a Franco-Chadian team led by Michel Brunet.
The central market of N'Djamena is commonly called 'souk kabir'.

blocks.prompt: About how many people do you think live in N'Djamena (the 2009 census)?

parts.text: 993,492 in 2009, according to the figures compiled from the national statistics office. Which area is counted matters: Ville de N'Djamena (ten arrondissements, 64 quartiers) at the 2009 second national census (RGPH2); other publications give 951,418 or 963,657 for the same census.

items.text: The French founded the city as Fort Lamy.
Fort-Lamy had its first mosque, in front of the governor's office.
A mosque was built from the local budget in the centre of Fort-Lamy.
King Faisal of Saudi Arabia visited Chad at President Tombalbaye's invitation.
Tombalbaye renamed Fort Lamy as N'Djamena.
The Toumaï skull was found in the Djourab desert by a Franco-Chadian team.
The second census counted 993,492 inhabitants in the city.
The National Museum moved into a modern purpose-built complex near the National Assembly and the National Library.
UNESCO declared the Lakes of Ounianga the first World Heritage Site of Chad.
The central market was left without electricity for almost two weeks.
